newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ashton confirms Indian sales plan.
newsitem.headline: Ashton confirms Indian sales plan.

text.p: Australian diamond miner Ashton Mining Ltd said on Wednesday that it would continue to work closely with the Indian cutting and polishing industry as part of the market direct sales policy.

"Argyle sees a bright future as part of the Indian market and will continue strengthening its established strategic links with our Indian customers," Ashton quoted general manager commercial, Mark Hooper, as telling a diamond conference in South Africa.
Ashton owns 40 percent of Argyle Diamonds, the world's largest diamond mine, in a joint venture the RTZ-CRA Group which holds the other 60 percent.

Argyle said it had recently opened a new office in Antwerp to manage direct market sales with sales through this office focussed on meeting the needs of Indian rough diamond customers who purchase most of the Argyle rough product.
In June, the company said it would sell its stones direct to market in a rebuff for the huge diamond-selling cartel run by South Africa's De Beers group.
Ashton said market monitoring had indicated that the programme had resulted in significant sales growth and a marked lift in the competitive position of the Indian manufacturers.
At 10.40 a.m. (0030 GMT), Ashton shares were two cents higher at A$1.60 on turnover of 63,065 shares.
The Indo Argyle Diamond Council (IADC) was formed in 1994 to facilitate the emerging diamond jewellery production in Mumbai that was destined for the U.S. market.

Ashton said Argyle had also assisted by providing technical and marketing assistance to the members of the IADC with market monitoring of this programme indicating it had resulted in significant sales growth for Indian manufacturers and a marked lift in their competitive position.
